issue.title: Thread safety and Pytest
issue.body:
(This is a high-level issue that proposes making pytest more thread safe; I'm definitely looking for feedback, discussion, and confirmation this is a good direction here.) ### Background This issue comes out of a brief conversation on the pytest discord: > [@ngoldbaum] out of curiosity, if there were funding for work on improving pytest’s thread safety, is that something that the project might be interested in? For the work we’ve been doing so far we’ve contracted David Woods to work on Cython, David Hewitt to work on PyO3, and Liam DeVoe to work on Hypothesis. Is there an opportunity for pytest as well? > [@The-Compiler] Personally I'm not too interested in it being thread-safe, but I'd absolutely support using our Opencollective funds to make it happen > [@ronnypfannschmidt] my sentinent is the same - but i also want to note that i'd prefer thread safety in a manner that uses queues and non-shared state for fixtures & co (aka xdist-alike, just without separate node objects) - the key contention would be log/stdio capture state + managing pytest stores on nodes in a controlled manner I don't presume to know the best direction for thread-safety in pytest, so I'm opening this issue to get some feedback on my understanding. While this may be obvious to all involved, I want to at least give a brief motivation for thread-safety here. Python is working towards removing the [global interpreter lock](https://docs.python.org/3/glossary.html#term-global-interpreter-lock), in a python build version called [free-threading](https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/). As free-threading progresses, it seems likely that more people will want to run multiple tests simultaneously in separate threads. In particular, it would be nice for free-threading development if [pytest-xdist](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist) supported threading (in place of multiprocessing) as its worker primitive, so existing test suites can be run with pytest-xdist in threading mode to flush out concurrency bugs.

Initial proposal

 ### Proposal I would summarize all of pytest as two (very complex) steps: 1. Test collection. 2. Test execution. with some calls to [pluggy](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy) thrown in during both. From talking with @zac-hd, I understand there's some appetite for parallelizing collection in pytest itself using threads, perhaps as a consequence of folding pytest-xdist into pytest. This would require making (1) test collection thread safe. I think that parallelized test collection is "merely" a performance improvement, so I'm not proposing it in this issue, though it may be something to keep in mind. Instead I want to focus on (2); making test execution thread-safe. Here is my understanding of the required work there: - [ ] Make pluggy thread-safe, as hooks will be called from multiple threads. - It's possible this work is either minimal or zero, if pluggy is already thread safe. - [ ] Guarantee all (feasible) built-in fixtures are thread-safe. - I don't (yet) know pytest internals enough to judge how difficult this will be. - Some fixtures, like `monkeypatch` and `capsys`, don't seem possible to make thread-safe. Perhaps someone knows an arcanely cursed way to achieve this? - [ ] Make pytest data collection during tests thread-safe. - the tracking of the number of xfails, successes, failures, etc. - [ ] Document the thread-safety guarantees, including what is and is not safe. - [ ] Add an opt-in execution model to pytest-xdist which uses threads instead of processes. - If we're done our job right up to this point, this should be *conceptually* simple, though it may require some involved changes to pytest-xdist to support this. And finally; - [ ] Test the heck out of this. - I put a substantial amount of effort into testing thread-safety when migrating Hypothesis: https://github.com/HypothesisWorks/hypothesis/pull/4489. I would expect to do so again here, though I don't yet know the best way to do so. ### Open questions - If we do leave fixtures like `monkeypatch` thread-unsafe, how should this interact with pytest-xdist's proposed threading mode? A few options: do nothing; print a warning; error; or skip the test. I don't like half of these! cc: @ngoldbaum, @lysnikolaou
### Refined Proposal - [ ] separate `SetupState` from `Session` - [ ] one `Session` collection-tree should be shared among all threads - [ ] each thread gets a separate `SetupState` and therefore a separate instance of each fixture - [ ] audit `Stash` uses for thread-safety - [ ] audit [`cacheprovider`](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/cache.html#the-new-config-cache-object) for thread-safety - [ ] make `capsys` thread-aware, with integrations for the per-thread `SetupState` ### Issues and PRs - https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13844 - https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/pull/13837

   - multithraded pytest will need stand-in objects with context locals
- collection thread safety is not necessarily required, its ok to leave it as a secondary concern

- sheduler protocols in process can be more powerful than xdist due to direct data access
- execution thread safety will require a more elaborate sheduling mechanism than modifyitems

I expect that we'll also see some improvements elsewhere in the ecosystem which make this easier, e.g. [here's a proposal](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/130148#issuecomment-2666553480) for `contextlib.redirect_stdout()` to become thread-aware which we'd be able to use (eventually).

I was also worried about warnings, but it seems that [`catch_warnings` is handled](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/warnings.html#warning-concurrent-safe) in Python 3.14, so pytest's warnings plugin should work at least.

Do I understand correctly that the idea here is that collection is done in a non-parallel phase on the main thread, and the same collection tree is shared among multiple parallel runners? As opposed to xdist which runs collection per worker.

> I was also worried about warnings, but it seems that catch_warnings is handled in Python 3.14, so pytest's warnings plugin should work at least.

And in-practice I haven't seen any thread safety issues due to uses of `pytest.warns` in 3.14, so any remaining thread safety issues in pytest itself should be hard to trigger, if there are any.

Thanks for the discussion here. Here's a more refined todolist:

- [ ] separate `SetupState` from `Session`
  - [ ] one `Session` collection-tree should be shared among all threads
  - [ ] each thread gets a separate `SetupState` and therefore a separate instance of each fixture
- [ ] audit `Stash` uses for thread-safey
- [ ] make `capsys` thread-aware, with integrations for the per-thread `SetupState`

The working goal in my mind is to enable pytest support for the following implementation of a parallel `pytest_runtestloop`:

```python
from queue import Queue, Empty
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

n = 2

def pytest_runtestloop(session):
    queue = Queue()
    for item in session.items:
        queue.put(item)

    def worker():
        try:
            item = queue.get_nowait()
        except Empty:
            return

        while item is not None:
            try:
                next_item = queue.get_nowait()
            except Empty:
                next_item = None

            item.config.hook.pytest_runtest_protocol(
                item=item, nextitem=next_item
            )
            item = next_item

    with ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
        futures = [executor.submit(worker) for _ in range(n)]
        for future in futures:
            future.result()

    return True
```

which could be implemented by e.g. [pytest-run-parallel](https://github.com/Quansight-Labs/pytest-run-parallel) or a simplified pytest-xdist as they see fit. (I thought implementing this parallelism in a plugin might require additional pytest hooks, but I think `pytest_runtestloop` covers it.)

I don't think Quansight or @ngoldbaum necessarily sees it as a requirement that pytest itself ship such a parallel execution model, merely that pytest makes it possible to implement one, though feel free to correct me. As a result, I don't think we yet have to address concerns like "monkeypatch is inherently thread-unsafe", because that can be a caveat/requirement of writing such a parallel `pytest_runtestloop`. But if we did, then an extension is:

- [ ] figure out what to do about inherently-unsafe fixtures like `monkeypatch`
  - [ ] possibly by requiring each fixture to opt-{in, out} to thread safety

[I also forgot to mention in the original post, but #13679 would be wonderful to have merged for pytest-run-parallel!]

Liam's summary seems like an excellent plan and would substantially help ecosystem efforts to improve multithreaded test coverage. Currently there's lots of manual patching that's needed to work around pytest thread safety issues that Liam's plan would fix. If each thread had a local fixture and if setup and teardown happened in a thread-safe manner, @bwhitt7's recent work on using pytest-run-parallel [in the NumPy CI](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/29552) would have been a lot easier, just as a concrete example. Pairing pytest-run-parallel with compiler sanitizers is already pointing out [real bugs](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/29890).

Thanks all for your active participation and ideas on this thread, I'm really excited about where this can go.

To limit the scope of this, I think we should limit the usage of ``--threads`` (just gonna assume that will be the flag 😀 ) to the freethreaded build. The reasons being:

- Without free threading the feature is probably not so useful (not *useless*, but less useful for the main purpose of speeding up the test suite).
 
- It allows us to focus on a new Python baseline (e.g. no Python 3.10 headaches).
 
- The free threaded build enables two very relevant flags by default, `sys.flags.thread_inherit_context` and `sys.flags.context_aware_warnings`. See [here](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/20b69aac0d19a5e5358362410d9710887762f0e7/Doc/howto/free-threading-python.rst#behavioral-changes) (python docs are currently 503 so linking to github instead).

---

With `sys.flags.thread_inherit_context` I think we can make a usable `capsys` replacement using `ContextVar`. Using `threading.local` alone wouldn't be good since it will fail to capture in tests which themselves launch threads.

Using `ContextVar` is problematic as well, tests which launch threads or tasks without inheriting the context will then fail to capture. For threads with the `sys.flags.thread_inherit_context` I'd be less worried. Async tests probably do this more, although I think even `asyncio.run` inherits context from the running thread, so maybe it's fine.

---

> each thread gets a separate SetupState and therefore a separate instance of each fixture

Liam's idea to have entirely separate SetupState's is the simplest way, similar to how xdist works. Is it workable in practice?

What I think Ronny is aiming at is for threads to share higher-scope fixtures. This will bring a significant advantage over xdist, but will no longer be a "shared nothing" architecture, so a significant up in the complexity. Also due to setup/teardown expectations, it will have heavy synchronization overhead and basically serialize the threads in some cases, unless the scheduler (what assigns tests to threads) is smart enough to avoid that. (And don't forget higher-scoped fixtures can be parametrized, meaning setup/torndown multiple times.)

An update - here's my current progress on thread safety: https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/compare/main...Liam-DeVoe:pytest:threading-work?expand=1. 

This branch requires each thread that runs `runtestprotocol` to follow a `pytest-thread-{n}` naming convention, which pytest uses to track that thread as a "pytest thread". This branch uses `ContextVar` and assumes [`thread_inherit_context=1`](https://docs.python.org/3/using/cmdline.html#envvar-PYTHON_THREAD_INHERIT_CONTEXT) is set, so that threads spawned by tests inherit knowledge of the current "pytest thread" and integrate accordingly.

In this branch, each pytest thread gets its own copy of each fixture's value. Fixtures are effectively thread-local. (*they are really *pytest-thread*-local, as threads spawned inside tests still use that pytest thread's fixture value).

Note that I think this is a somewhat less structural refactoring than the separation of `SetupState` and `Session` which has been suggested in this thread. I'm curious to hear thoughts on this, and whether this should go further in refactoring pytest internals.

---

I'm pretty excited to report that this branch lets me run most of the Hypothesis test suite in parallel, when combined with the appropriate `conftest.py`:

<details>

```python
import threading
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from queue import Empty, Queue

n = 3


def pytest_runtestloop(session):
    queue = Queue()
    for item in session.items:
        queue.put(item)

    def worker(worker_id):
        threading.current_thread().name = f"pytest-thread-{worker_id}"
        try:
            item = queue.get_nowait()
        except Empty:
            return

        while item is not None:
            try:
                next_item = queue.get_nowait()
            except Empty:
                next_item = None

            item.config.hook.pytest_runtest_protocol(item=item, nextitem=next_item)
            item = next_item

    with ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
        futures = [executor.submit(worker, i) for i in range(n)]
        for future in futures:
            future.result()

    return True
```

</details>

Stumbling blocks are that it currently requires `--capture no -p no:cacheprovider`. The former will definitely require some work to fix, whereas I'm merely somewhat skeptical of the latter's thread-safety, and am keeping it out of an abundance of caution for now.
